name: Caelrun
tagline: Lakeside fishing village that feeds the Marches, and does not ask who lets it.

population.mix: Mostly fisherfolk; barley farmers along the shore; fringe camps at the bog edge.

ruler: No lord. The great families rule in practice: the Hallans (the fleet) and the Tarnes (the grain).
strangers: Welcome for trade. Some things are carefully not asked about, and strangers who ask are noticed.

far: the lake flat and grey beyond the barley
near: racks hung with split fish, smoking
leaving: fish smell in your clothes for days
the reed beds closing behind the road

dusk: boats coming in low with the catch

night: reeds rustling where there is no wind
on moonless nights, a green-blue glow over the northern deep

winter: eel traps set under the ice
summer: old temple columns showing in the shallows in drought

itself.title: Food for the Marches
itself.text: Fish, eels, and barley from Caelrun feed the other Marches villages. Dried and smoked fish, fish oil, rush mats, and lake-hemp rope go out along the road. Caelrun has no smith of its own; iron, tools, and boat-nails come in by caravan.

itself.title: By lizard-man sufferance
itself.text: The swamp around Caelrun is lizard-man country, and the village survives because they allow it. Most residents believe their prosperity comes from hard work and good land. Sarith the Watcher, Brecht Hallan, and Ordun Tarnes know the compact's real shape and keep it unspoken.

itself.title: Debt-bound
itself.text: Debts pass from father to son here. Bound labourers work them off in the oil pits, and the village does not protect anyone who runs.

itself.title: Ruins under the lake
itself.text: The Submerged Temple-Garden lies in the northern deep. Its columns show in the shallows in a dry summer, and on moonless nights the water over it glows. The Aurka are diving it; the elders know exploring it is limited by the compact.

day: **Essa the Net-Mender** offers a piece of gossip, and wants one back.
Two families argue on the walkway over whose net it is.
A boat comes in with a strange catch, and a crowd gathers.
**2d4 militia** make a drunken patrol along the walkways.
A stranger with ink-stained hands is quietly buying anything old from the lake.
**3 Aurka** from a rival team load diving gear into a hired boat.
night: **Kelvan Bresul**, drunk, tells a war story at the Waterside Tavern.
Bresul boats slip out without lanterns, low in the water.
**Yavra Quickwater** waits at the Main Jetty for a passenger.
Green-blue light over the northern deep, brighter than last time.
A **lizard-man** stands at the reed line, watching, and is gone when looked at again.
**Dren** sits on the oil-pit wall, counting something on his fingers.

response.watch: About 20 ceremonial militia under Kelvan Bresul, mostly good for drunks and disputes.
response.arrival_night: 1d3 militia within 1d4 turns, if Kelvan can be roused.
response.reinforcements: A handful of old veterans, if anyone thinks to call them.
response.bribery: Easily: a few coppers and a good story.
response.strength: Ceremonial. The real protection is the lizard-men, and almost no one knows it.

locations.name: Silver Perch Inn
locations.look: An inn on stilts overlooking the docks, run by the Hallans.

labels.guests: Taziri's caravan and whoever travels with it.
labels.services: Rooms over the water; lake fish and barley bread. Prices pending OSRIC 3.0 table.

locations.name: Waterside Tavern
locations.look: The village tavern, on the water and loud every night.

labels.guests: Fishers, militia, and their drinking captain.
labels.trouble: War stories of dubious accuracy; fishing-rights quarrels spill onto the walkway.

locations.name: Dockside Market
locations.look: Stalls on the dock where the catch is sold and the Norvaks negotiate caravan trade.

labels.days: Every morning; market day draws the whole lake.

locations.name: The Fishmonger's
locations.hidden: A back room where Ossek Thrice-Buried does the accounts as cover. It is a node in the Aurka network.

locations.name: Guild Hall
locations.look: The net-menders' and rope-makers' hall, and the village's real exchange for gossip.

labels.services: Nets and lake-hemp rope of good quality.

locations.name: The Oil Pits
locations.look: Fish-oil rendering vats, visible from the walkways and smelled from everywhere.

labels.off_the_books: Worked by debt-bound labourers; debts are bought and sold like barrels.

locations.name: Boatwright's Yard
locations.look: Sawdust, pitch, and hulls on trestles.

labels.wares: Fishing boats built to last decades.
labels.proprietor: Tovar the boatwright, who will not be rushed.

locations.name: Shrine of Thulda
locations.look: A small grey shrine where the dead are prepared.

labels.populace: Mourners, and Mother Hildreth spinning wool by the door.

locations.name: Hallan Compound
locations.look: The fleet master's family compound by the main jetty.

labels.inhabitants: Brecht Hallan, about 40 kin, and servants under Penna.

locations.name: Tarnes Granary
locations.look: Barley stores above the shore fields.

locations.name: Main Jetty
locations.look: The boat landing at the heart of the village.

labels.passage: Boats to the decaying dock on the southwest shore, then the swamp path: 6 miles by water and 3 on foot to Nebruz. Yavra Quickwater ferries, for a price and no questions.

locations.name: Decaying Dock
locations.look: A half-sunk dock on the southwest shore where the swamp path begins.

labels.passage: Swamp path to Nebruz, 3 miles on foot through lizard-man country. Will-o'-wisps have been seen.

locations.name: The Marsh Edge
locations.look: Leech pools, fringe camps, Kessa's hut, and Varren's stilted shack where the lake turns to swamp.
locations.hidden: Night channels through the swamp toward Nebruz.

locations.name: Far-Shore Reed Hut
locations.look: Brother Kellis's reed hut on the far shore, ringed with cairns that mark the safe water paths.

labels.inhabitants: Brother Kellis. Travellers leave offerings at the cairns before crossing.

locations.name: The Drowned Columns
locations.look: Temple pillars that break the surface in a dry summer, about 800 yards north of the fishing grounds.

labels.custom: Fishers steer around them; fish avoid the water there.

factions.membership: Ossek's node in the fishmonger's back room; Varren Muddfoot informs.
factions.scheme: Diving the Submerged Temple-Garden; stopped at its sealed lead door. A rival team is preparing too.

factions.membership: Three tendencies: the Clean Death, the Restrained Hunger, the Long Work.
factions.scheme: Watch from the reeds, and answer any breach of the compact. Not quickly, not obviously, but surely.
Watching the temple ruins from a distance.

trouble: Aurka activity at the ruins is drawing unwanted attention, and a rival team is preparing its own dive.
The lizard-man compact is unspoken; a major expedition into the temple would breach it.
Dren, debt-bound at the oil pits, wants to run to Nebruz. The Norvaks will pursue, and the village won't protect him.
Bresul boats make midnight trips, carrying something.
Tobacco, by way of Mother Yaleth, has caught on among the militia.
Fringe workers at the bog edge live outside village authority.

neighbors.notes: 6 miles by boat through the swamp channels, then 3 miles on foot through lizard-man swamp.

defenses.militia: Ceremonial, mostly for disputes and drunk fishers
defenses.reality: Lizard-men enforce territorial boundaries from shadows
defenses.village_understanding: Most residents believe their prosperity comes from hard work and good location, unaware of the arrangement

trade_focus: Food surplus provider - feeds other Marches villages

legacy_rumours: Aurka found carved stones in submerged temple foundations
Old temple columns visible in shallows during summer droughts
dm_notes.campaign_state: As of session 27: the party passed through with Taziri's caravan, met Yavra Quickwater, then went Caelrun, decaying dock, swamp path, Nebruz, Leeandra's hut. Leeandra is brewing water-breathing potions in exchange for giant constrictor brain fluid. The party has not yet dived the Submerged Temple-Garden. Their Aurka contact is Ossek, not Varren.
dm_notes.temple_notes: Western Wing beyond a sealed lead door: a greater wight hierophant conducting Nanna-Sin's liturgy alone, who wants to give someone the Tablets of the Reckoning (the Silence was a timed alignment and will recur). The ruins glow when the 300-year-old preservation enchantments are stressed. Full room-by-room writeup lives in Andrew's local site_submerged_temple_garden.md, not yet in the repo.
